messages.subject: Issues trying to learn secr coding to estimate fox densities
messages.subject_clean: Issues trying to learn secr coding to estimate fox densities
messages.body_plain:
Hello, I'm really struggling to use secr to find fox densities from camera trap data. I am a beginner to RStudio.

Currently, I seem to have read my capture and
trap data in okay, using txt files. I ran read.capthist and for a change got no
errors. Then I attempted to plot the capthist and it did it, but I thought it
stange that when I plotted it, the data points are not on the detectors, is this right?

I then
copied and pasted some code for plotting a histogram of sucessive movement and
it all came out as zero. I don't know whether any of the foxes were recorded on
multiple cameras without looking but not sure if this would present a problem.
When asking for a quick and biased estimate of sigma (which I don't understand)
it also came out as zero. I tried fitting the model anyway using

fit <- secr.fit (sumbadsouth.secr, buffer = 1000 *
initialsigma, trace = FALSE)

##resulting in the following:

Warning: no points in mask Warning in autoini(capthist = ch,
mask = msk, binomN = tempbinomN, adjustg0 = details$binomN[1] == : 'dbar' close
to zero; using detector spacing instead Warning: 'secr.fit' failed because
initial values not found (data sparse?); specify transformed values in 'start'

I then copied and pasted code to create a mask:

```{r}
Spiti.mask.sumbadsouth<-make.mask(traps(sumbadsouth.secr), buffer = 300,
type = "trapbuffer") Spiti.sumbadsouth.hhn <-
secr.fit(sumbadsouth.secr, model = list(D~1, lambda0~1, sigma~1), detectfn =
"HHN", mask = Spiti.mask.sumbadsouth) ```

##resulting in the following:

Checking data Preparing detection design matrices Preparing
density design matrix Finding initial parameter values...

Warning in autoini(capthist = ch, mask = msk, binomN =
tempbinomN, adjustg0 = details$binomN[1] == : 'dbar' close to zero; using
detector spacing instead Warning: 'secr.fit' failed because initial values not
found (data sparse?); specify transformed values in 'start'

I also tried with 'detectfn = HN" and got another different error.

I really hope this doesn't mean I don't have enough data! Apologies
for the long post, I'd be really grateful if someone could help.

Gaz

messages.subject: Re: Issues trying to learn secr coding to estimate fox densities
messages.subject_clean: Issues trying to learn secr coding to estimate fox densities
messages.body_plain:
Without diving in too deeply -
My guess is this: 'secr' expresses all distances in metres. The plot method for capthist objects places the detections on successive occasions at a certain radial distance from the detector location (argument 'rad', default 5 ). This makes sense for  brushtail possums, but not for all other cases! Usually it just means rad is too small but if you have (i) expressed distances in km or (ii) failed to project data from lat-lon then you'll get strange results.
Murray

messages.subject: Comparing density estimates
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have conducted a follow-up camera trapping study to one conducted 2-years prior in the same study area, replicating the exact methods, study design etc. I am comparing density estimates for a species between the two studies using SECR.

I decided that the EX detection function was a better fit for my data (whereas the previous study used HN as the better fit). Density estimates are not significantly different between HN and EX for my data, but is it better scientific practice to use the same detection function for better comparability, or is it more important that the chosen detection function is the best possible fit to the data? (since AIC is highest for the HN function)

I appreciate any advice on this issue.

Edie

messages.subject: Re: Using secr.fit with a habitat mask leads to error - "Warning: missing values in predictors?Error in lpred[, 1] <- Yp : replacement has length zero"
messages.subject_clean: Using secr.fit with a habitat mask leads to error - "Warning: missing values in predictors?Error in lpred[, 1] <- Yp : replacement has length zero"
messages.body_plain:
Update:

For those who may also encounter this, I figured out my error was because I coded something like:
secr.fit(model = list(D ~ scale(covariate name), lambda0 ~ h2, sigma ~ h2))

Error in lpred[, 1] <- Yp : replacement has length zero In addition: Warning message: missing values in predictors?

No errors when scale() is removed from the model list:
secr.fit(model = list(D ~ covariate name, lambda0 ~ h2, sigma ~ h2))

This fashion was from the author of package spOccupancy, which allows you to scale covariates while modeling and reduces a few lines of codes.

However for secr, it will result in an error at this moment.

Hope this helps
